report:
Right ovary and fallopian tube

Received in a fresh state is a right salpingo-oophorectomy specimen received intact. The ovarian mass measures 120 mm in greatest dimension and weighs 350 g. The outer surface bears papillary excrescences. Cut surface shows solid areas and necrosis. Representative sections of the solid and papillary areas are embedded in 2 frozen blocks and subsequently converted to paraffin blocks. The fallopian tube is unremarkable.

(1-6) Ovarian tumour, including surface.
(7) Fallopian tube, entirely embedded (SEE-FIM).

Malignant; carcinoma, favour high-grade serous carcinoma.

The paraffin section confirms the frozen section diagnosis. It shows features of high-grade serous carcinoma.

Specimen and tumour
- Procedure: Right salpingo-oophorectomy
- Specimen integrity (right ovary): Capsule intact
- Specimen integrity (right fallopian tube): Serosa intact
- Tumour site: Right tubo-ovarian
- Ovarian surface involvement: Present, right
- Fallopian tube surface involvement: Not identified
- Tumour size: 120 mm in greatest dimension

Microscopic findings
- Histologic type: High-grade serous carcinoma
- Histologic grade: Not applicable (high grade by definition)
- Tumour histology:
  Sections show a high-grade serous carcinoma. The tumour grows in solid sheets
  punctuated by slit-like spaces, with hierarchical papillary branching and
  cribriform and glandular areas. The cells are cuboidal to columnar with
  eosinophilic cytoplasm and markedly pleomorphic, hyperchromatic nuclei
  including bizarre and multinucleated forms, with large eosinophilic nucleoli.
  Mitotic figures are numerous and include atypical forms, geographic and
  comedo-type necrosis is present, and tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes and
  psammoma bodies are seen. The fallopian tube mucosa is involved by invasive
  carcinoma. The fimbrial mucosa shows a focus of serous tubal intraepithelial
  carcinoma, in which the epithelium is stratified and denuded of ciliated
  cells, with loss of nuclear polarity, enlarged hyperchromatic pleomorphic
  nuclei, prominent nucleoli and epithelial fractures with exfoliation of small
  cell clusters, without stromal invasion. Immunohistochemistry: p53 shows an
  abnormal pattern (strong diffuse nuclear overexpression); WT1 positive, PAX8
  positive.
- Lymphovascular invasion: Present
- p53 immunohistochemistry: Abnormal, Overexpression (strong, diffuse nuclear
  expression, more than 90%)
- Largest extrapelvic peritoneal focus: Not applicable
- Peritoneal / ascitic fluid: Malignant cells present
- Other tissue / organ involvement: Not identified

Lymph nodes
- Regional lymph nodes: Not submitted

Distant metastasis
- Distant metastasis: Not identified

Additional findings
- Serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC)

OVARY AND FALLOPIAN TUBE, right, salpingo-oophorectomy x frozen section
- HIGH-GRADE SEROUS CARCINOMA, tubo-ovarian, 120 mm, ovarian surface involved;
  see synoptic report
- peritoneal fluid positive for malignant cells; lymphovascular invasion present
